items.text: Its legislators vote to keep in place the existing tax system, in which tax revenue equals about 44 percent of annual economic output, the top tax rate on earnings is about 55 percent, starting at about 13 times the average wage, and the tax rate on company profits is about 26 percent.

Its legislators vote to keep in place the existing rules, in which the minimum wage is about 62 percent of the median full-time wage, collective agreements cover about 98 percent of employees, and an employer needs a real and serious reason and a formal procedure to dismiss an employee, must give one to two months' notice after six months of service, and must pay severance of at least a quarter of a month's pay per year of service, with court awards for unfair dismissal capped on a scale.

items.text: Its legislators passed, as the only group voting for it, a budget amendment raising the tax on companies' purchases of their own shares from 8 to 33 percent and extending it to more companies.

Proposed replacing the tax on property wealth with a tax on financial wealth that excludes business assets, small-company shares, and middle-class housing, and opposed raising the tax rate on investment income.
